properties.chose: KEPT AS INTENT 2026-09-25 on Anthony's word ("yes, let's keep this as intent"), in the sharpened shape from the Anthony–Alex discussion: the design lives in its reflow2 server (local or hosted), the code repository carries nothing of reflow2's beyond an optional MCP config and agent file, the export is automatic to a destination the owner chooses (the code repo being one option), and reflow2 keeps the design↔implementation link. That is (c) with owner-chosen export, which subsumes (b) and (d); (a) is not taken. Became req:a-design-lives-in-its-server-not-in-the-code-repo and req:the-design-saves-itself-wherever-the-owner-chooses. req:persistence (accepted) conflicts and awaits Anthony's word on retiring or rewording it.
properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL (2026-09-25, from the dev_reflow2 hub session).

In Anthony's words: "Right now, in all my projects, my reflow2 design objects are in the same repo as the implementation. This is nice in some ways - particularly because if somebody git clones my project's repo, they get both the reflow2 design and the implementation of that design. ... I'm starting to think the better approach is to keep reflow2 design in a separate location from the implementation of design. ... for public codebases like bluesky or ophyd-async or many others, ... I'm saying to 'gitignore the reflow2 design object' so that it doesn't get pushed in PRs to the upstream github repos. Instead, I'm thinking it might be better to just keep the reflow2 design object in the mcp server (and either export it to its own folder or simply keep it on the server until I want to transfer). ... maybe if one day, everybody in the world uses reflow2 and it is accepted to have a reflow2 design object in your repo and people know what that is, then we can resume keeping the design in the same repo as the implementation, but for now, nobody really knows what reflow2 is, so putting a design object into a project like bluesky that is used around the world is a no-go."

WHERE IT CAME FROM: two hubs (hxm_program at work, over nine NSLS2 repos; dev_reflow2 here, over reflow2, flo2 and cure) that act as CLIENTS of several projects at once, and the 2026-09-25 flo2 brainstorm on where implemented artifacts live.

═══ OPTIONS, NONE CHOSEN ═══
(a) KEEP IT IN THE REPO — today's shape (req:persistence) — and git-ignore it wherever the upstream will not accept it.
(b) A DESIGN REPOSITORY OF ITS OWN, beside each implementation or one per hub. It holds the export, the per-node merge rule and the CI design gate; the design points at the implementation by repository, path and commit.
(c) THE DESIGN LIVES ON A SERVER (flo2.io / api.flo2.io, or a self-hosted reflow2) and is exported to a folder of its own when wanted.
(d) PER PROJECT: in the repo for projects the owner controls, outside it for everyone else's — asked once, at install or adopt.

═══ SHARPENED 2026-09-25, SAME SESSION — STILL RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING ═══
FROM A DISCUSSION BETWEEN ANTHONY AND ALEX (who:alex), relayed by Anthony into this session. Which sentences are whose was not said, so the passage is attributed to both: "I'm starting to feel that keeping the design in the reflow2 mcp server and the implementation of code in its repo is the better approach ... In some ways, I would want nothing related to reflow2 in my code repo, except maybe a config file enabling the MCP server and the agents MD file letting it know to use it for designs. For work, it still needs to be something I can git commit though or at least something I can save somewhere that I choose. The reflow2 mcp server would have the design and it would still be exportable to wherever you like. So you could potentially leave it on the server and only export when you want, need, or to backup. You could probably even say, export to the same repo as the implemented design, but this becomes optional where and how you want to export your design. In any case, the linkage between design and implementation must be maintained by reflow2."

THE SHAPE THIS NAMES: the design's home is the reflow2 server (local or hosted); the code repo holds at most an MCP config and an agent-instructions file; export goes wherever the owner chooses, the code repo being one option among several; and reflow2 owns the design↔implementation link (dec:idea-a-design-apart-from-its-code-knows-where-its-implementation-is).

CLAUDE CODE'S ASSESSMENT, given when asked: agree, on three conditions. (1) Export must stay AUTOMATIC to the chosen destination — reflow2 already writes its export through on every change, so only the destination moves; if export becomes something to remember, the Aug-5 "default flip" costs designs. (2) The link must be first-class before the move, and out-of-tree measurement fixed. (3) For upstream projects even the MCP config and agent file can live in user- or machine-level configuration, so the repo carries nothing at all.
properties.name: A reflow2 design lives in its server, apart from the code it describes, and saves itself wherever its owner chooses
properties.rationale:
⭐ THE STRONGEST ARGUMENT IS ANTHONY'S OWN, AND IT MAKES (a) ALREADY UNTRUE FOR THE CASES THAT PROMPTED THIS. The live store (.reflow2/graph) has always been git-ignored; the export is what persists. Git-ignore the export too, as Anthony does for bluesky and ophyd-async, and the design exists only in one laptop's store, with no durable copy anywhere. req:persistence ("the design travels with the repo") is silently not met for exactly those projects today.

⚠️ IT IS NOT ONLY THE DESIGN FILE. reflow2's installer also writes AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md, .mcp.json, and a .gitattributes merge rule into the implementation repo. All of them are things an upstream maintainer would not accept in a PR either. Separation has to cover the installer's whole footprint, not just docs/design/.

WHAT SEPARATION COSTS, recorded beside it:
· "git clone gets both" — the property Anthony values — is lost under (b) and (c): a reader needs two clones, or a link.
· The CI design gate runs in the implementation repo's CI today. Separated, it runs in the design's home and has to check out the implementation to measure it.
· Artifact locations stop being paths in one tree and become claims about another repository at a commit. Part of this is already built: a registered file is measured under a configurable project root (cap:a-registered-file-is-measured-under-the-project-root-and-the-record-says-measured-or-asserted), and the hubs already hold per-machine paths. What is missing is recording WHICH repository and commit an artifact lives in. flo2's twelve schema artifacts that point into reflow2's repository and read as unmeasurable are this problem in miniature.
· (c) on its own gives up git history, per-node merge and review-by-PR, unless exports are committed somewhere. So (c) is really (b) with a server in front: the server as the working medium, a design repository as the durable record — option (c) of dec:idea-package-versus-shared-server arrived at from the other side.

THE AUG-5 FINDING STILL HOLDS AND NARROWS THIS: the package was always the EXPORT, never the store. Separation changes where the export is committed, not what it is.

COST, as a finding: (d) is the smallest change — a setting at install or adopt that decides where the installer writes. (b) is medium: a repository per design or per hub, and a cross-repository CI gate. (c) depends on flo2's hosted address.

REVISIT TRIGGER, in Anthony's words: "if one day, everybody in the world uses reflow2 and it is accepted to have a reflow2 design object in your repo".

Idea and field evidence are Anthony's; options, costs and pushback are Claude Code's.
